projects.title: Systems
projects.intro: Three systems in production, each solving a different problem. One of them cut 65% of the time the client’s team spent opening and approving work orders.
projects.client_intro: Institutional sites and conversion pages. The goal here was never a pretty portfolio — it was the client being found and getting contacted.
projects.junior-jets_desc: Marine services management ecosystem: work order flow, digital approval via unique link, and automated WhatsApp notifications.
projects.devburger_desc: Full ordering application for a burger restaurant: catalogue, cart, checkout and tracking panel. Order state is validated on the server, not on the screen — the interface may go stale, the order must never reach an impossible state.
projects.controleja_desc: Personal finance dashboard with its own JWT authentication. The owner filter lives in the query, not in the interface: a UI bug can never expose someone else’s entries.
projects.meu-caribe_desc: Institutional site for a tourism business in Maragogi, Brazil.
projects.clinica-vellys_desc: Aesthetics clinic site focused on booking and service presentation.
projects.nutricionista_desc: Landing page focused on conversion to WhatsApp booking.
projects.contest_intro: A full landing page redesign for a programming school, built for a contest. Result still under review.
projects.devclub_desc: Landing page for a programming school: 15 courses filterable by category, a project carousel, a salary comparator, an FAQ accordion and an animated canvas background. Long-form copy written from scratch.

about.title: About
about.lede: I’m a full-stack developer based in Maragogi, Brazil. I work the whole project — understand the problem, design the database, write the API, build the interface and ship it. On my own, start to finish.
about.edge_body: Most developers ship the screen. I ship what happens after it — automated WhatsApp notifications, webhooks that fire on their own, flows that run without anyone pressing a button. That's what cut 65% of the client's operational time on Junior Jets.

stack.title: Stack
stack.intro: Not a wall of logos. This is the architecture I actually build, layer by layer, and the reason behind each choice.
stack.interface_why: Server Components by default. JavaScript only where there's real interaction — everything else arrives as ready HTML.
stack.api_why: Typed contract end to end, with Zod validating at the edge and Next Route Handlers in front. The same schema runs on client and server, so they can’t drift apart.
stack.data_why: Relational when integrity is at stake, document when the schema is still moving. The choice comes from the problem, not from habit.
stack.automation_why: This is where most developers stop and I keep going. Webhooks, queues and the WhatsApp API so the system keeps working after I leave.
stack.infra_why: Reproducible deploys and preview per branch. If it doesn't ship with one command, it isn't ready.
